notes.subject: קץ/הקיץ
notes.rationale: Paronomasia: qeṣ (tagara) and heqiq (yessahder) share the root consonants q-ṣ; the end 'wakes up' — a pun impossible to keep in kab.

notes.subject: הקיץ אליך
notes.rationale: 'It awakens against you' (KJV 'watcheth for thee') vs 'it has roused itself against you' (BSB); the verb depicts the end as waking and rising up to strike.

notes.subject: ɣur-k
notes.rationale: Direct address to the one dwelling in the land — Israel/Jerusalem under judgment.

translation: Tagara tewweḍ, tagara tewweḍ; tecbeḍ ⟨k.cc⟩ ɣef ufella-nnek <texleq>? — ssehder ula d nettat: ssehder-it ɣur-k; wali, teṭṭef-ed abrid-ines, tusa-d.
